Whether you have medical debt, credit card debt, or just about any other kind of debt that goes to a collection agency (student loan and tax debt not included), the debt collectors have to follow what's called the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act - FDCPA.

In it, there is a laundry list of what a debt collector (not necessarily the company that originally owned the debt) absolutely cannot do. Those things include:

  • Continuing to call you after you've told them to stop either in writing or on the phone.
  • Calling you if you have a lawyer.
  • Calling you between 9:00pm and 8:00am your time.
  • Contacting you after you've requested validation of a debt but before they validate it.
  • Lying about who they are or anything in a conversation
  • Sending a postcard
  • Reporting information on your credit report that isn't true
  • Threatening legal action when they have no intention to do so.
  • Publishing your information on the internet
  • Fail to let you know you can dispute the debt
  • About a dozen other minor things - Typically anything remotely shady.

If they do, they would owe you $1,000 and your lawyer any legal fees you might incur.

Feel free to ask anything about this or the Fair Credit Reporting Act - FCRA, I've written extensively on the subject and I've seen people get decent paydays out of collection agencies.
[Debt] - What a debt collector can and cannot legally do to collect a debt

To add to this, don't be afraid to call a lawyer if something like this happened to you. Consumer protection attorneys love these kinds of cases because they are usually easy money, and they get to charge the other side $250 an hour. Usually you'll get a quick settlement offer if it's cut and dry.

One fun piece of advice: They have to verify you before they can say anything to you regarding said debt or account. Even if they know you are single, live by yourself, and call a phone number registered to you and publicly listed, when they start the call by saying "Mr such and such????", if you don't say "yes" they can't talk to you about this.

I'm not advocating not paying your debts, pay them. But you can still have fun with this answering the phone like "Jesus, how many times do I have to tell you people Mr. such and such is not at this number, have you ever heard of number being recycled?"
